messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: Install rmr2 in a local directory
parts:
Thanks for the excellent report and detailed analysis. I think you are right as far as what the problem is, but I don't have a solution. It will take some experiments and I suspect even a patch. I am on trip right now and with on and off internet access it's hard for me to look into this but I will give it a try late next week. If you are so advanced as to be willing to write a patch yourself, you can add a libpaths assignment just before line 148 ("invisible...") and see if that fixes it. It's a hack but it would tell me what is needed in a more acceptable solution. The other thing to worry about is if that path is available on every node in the cluster. It wouldn't be  the most common case of a cluster node with user directories mounted. Also make sure not to rely on ~ expansion, as the user as which the jobs are run is a special hadoop user, not your login user.


Antonio

On Friday, November 23, 2012 12:27:11 PM UTC+1, Claudio Reggiani wrote:
Hello,

I'm working on a computer in which I cannot have root permissions, so I managed to install all the packages required for rmr2_2.0.1 in ~/.Rlocal/.
The installation went ok, but I have some troubles while running jobs (with hadoop in pseudo mode)

this is the code I run (the $HADOOP_HOME is properly set)

.libPaths(c(.libPaths(), "/<path>/<to>/.Rlocal/"))
library("rmr2")
small.ints = to.dfs(1:1000)
out <- from.dfs(mapreduce(input = small.ints, map = function(k, v) cbind(v, v^2)))

The first three lines of code runs well, but in the last one I have this error

12/11/23 12:10:30 ERROR streaming.StreamJob: Job not successful. Error: # of failed Map Tasks exceeded allowed limit. FailedCount: 1. LastFailedTask: task_201211231209_0001_m_000000
12/11/23 12:10:30 INFO streaming.StreamJob: killJob...
Streaming Command Failed!
Error in mr(map = map, reduce = reduce, combine = combine, in.folder = if (is.list(input)) { :
  hadoop streaming failed with error code 1
Calls: from.dfs -> to.dfs.path -> mapreduce -> mr
Execution halted

Looking at some logs to get more information I found in stderr

Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'rmr2'
Calls: load ... tryCatch -> tryCatchList -> tryCatchOne -> <Anonymous>
Execution halted
java.lang.RuntimeException: PipeMapRed.waitOutputThreads(): subprocess failed with code 1
    at org.apache.hadoop.streaming.PipeMapRed.waitOutputThreads(PipeMapRed.java:362)
    at org.apache.hadoop.streaming.PipeMapRed.mapRedFinished(PipeMapRed.java:576)
    at org.apache.hadoop.streaming.PipeMapper.close(PipeMapper.java:135)
    at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapRunner.run(MapRunner.java:57)
    at org.apache.hadoop.streaming.PipeMapRunner.run(PipeMapRunner.java:36)
    at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.runOldMapper(MapTask.java:436)
    at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.run(MapTask.java:372)
    at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Child$4.run(Child.java:255)
    at java.security.AccessController.doPrivileged(Native Method)
    at javax.security.auth.Subject.doAs(Unknown Source)
    at org.apache.hadoop.security.UserGroupInformation.doAs(UserGroupInformation.java:1121)
    at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Child.main(Child.java:249)

I'm sure library("rmr2") works properly, but it sounds like to me that a 'child process' spawned by the father doesn't get .libPaths(c(.libPaths(), "/u/guestmlg/.Rlocal/"))

I'm working with rmr2 2.0.1, hadoop 1.0.3, CentOS distro 64bit

How do I solve this problem?
Thanks

On Monday, March 25, 2013 1:46:42 AM UTC-7, Vladimir Starostenkov wrote:
Hit the same issue. But I do have the root pass.
Installed rmr2, rhdfs from sources in the following way:
$cd /home/<username>
$git clone https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2.git

One comment about cloning. We changed our git workflow to follow what the git project does more closely (as opposed to git flows). So if you check out the project like this you get the current master which is somewhere between the current release and the next hotfix release. There is no guarantee how well tested that is. It's a stable version plus fixes, so that should be good, but we can't run the full battery of tests for every commit. The other thing is that you are going to run a non released version, somewhere in between 2.1.0 and 2.1.1, so if you need support it may be hard. So I encourage you to clone the project if you are not running in production, but if you experience problems, I suggest you go back to the latest stable. Thanks


Antonio
 
$sudo R CMD build ./rmr2/pkg/
$sudo R CMD INSTALL rmr2_2.1.0.tar.gz
Error, stderr are the same.

Streaming via
$hadoop jar $HADOOP_HOME/hadoop-0.20-mapreduce/contrib/streaming/hadoop-streaming-2.0.0-mr1-cdh4.2.0.jar <mapper, reducer etc.>
works fine.
